solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing; the grid proves the blog's answer wrong at 5 down, corrected here

entries.clue: Sport for a German, the paying supporter (6)

indicatorNotes.for a German: tells you to put the next word into German

blocks.note: sport can mean fun, as in 'in sport'

annotation.surface: A German fan who pays his way to back his favourite game.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sport' looks like a game to name, but it is fun, as in 'said in sport'.
annotation.definitionFit: A funder is someone who supports a cause or project by paying for it.

indicatorNotes.after: the result comes after the leading position in the down entry

blocks.note: an end is an outcome or result

annotation.surface: A match result is overturned on appeal after one side had been ahead.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is sport, where 'overturn a result' means an appeal; here 'Overturn' is the definition and the rest builds it.
annotation.definitionFit: To upend something is to turn it upside down, to overturn it.

indicatorNotes.raised: in a down clue, raising a word turns it upside down, so ANN reads NNA
indicatorNotes.charging: the girl charges into the fees, landing inside them

blocks.note: dues are fees, split around the girl

annotation.surface: Governesses who brought up a girl and billed the family for it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Raised' reads as brought up, the governess's job; in a down clue it means written upward.
annotation.definitionFit: A duenna is an older woman who acts as governess or chaperone to girls in a Spanish or Portuguese family.

blocks.note: a mission is a purpose or calling

annotation.surface: Something is reduced deliberately.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On purpose' reads as one phrase meaning deliberately; split it into two words for two pieces.
annotation.definitionFit: A remission is a lessening, as of a sentence or of the symptoms of a disease.

entries.clue: Chaps add up in their heads (8)

blocks.note: to tally is to add up

annotation.surface: Men doing sums without pen or paper.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is one sentence about mental arithmetic, and the answer describes exactly that.
annotation.definitionFit: Doing something mentally is doing it in your head.

indicatorNotes.off: GO comes off the fruit, leaving what remains

blocks.note: removed from the end of MANGO

annotation.surface: People lose their taste for fruit.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Go off' reads as a phrasal verb, to stop liking; here GO is the letters taken off. 'People' is the definition in the sense of mankind.
annotation.definitionFit: Man can mean people collectively, the human race.
annotation.definitionNote: 'People' is plural in form, but man in the sense of humankind is collective

indicatorNotes.requires: the phrase needs, and so contains, the answer

annotation.surface: The least amount of gas an airship needs to stay up.
annotation.walkthrough: A dirigible is an airship, and the surface is about filling one. Minimum is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Astronomers use the word for the point directly below the observer, and figuratively it is the lowest point anything reaches: a plain synonym.

entries.clue: Old hat caught under a rocking chair (7)

indicatorNotes.rocking: a rocking chair moves, so CHAIR is rearranged
indicatorNotes.under: in a down clue, C goes below the rest

annotation.surface: An old hat snagged beneath a rocking chair.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Old hat' looks like a thing under the chair; it is an idiom for out of date. 'Rocking chair' is a real object but here rocking tells you to jumble CHAIR.
annotation.definitionFit: Something old hat is old-fashioned, and archaic means belonging to an older time.

blocks.note: to ditch something is to scrap it

annotation.surface: Someone desperate refuses to stop fighting.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Scrap' reads as a fight, suiting 'desperate'; here it is the verb meaning throw away.
annotation.definitionFit: A last-ditch effort is a desperate final attempt.

blocks.note: settled or fixed, as a fact found out

annotation.surface: A company that has been trading for years.
annotation.walkthrough: Read together, the clue is 'an established firm', a long-standing company; split it into two adjectives.
annotation.definitionFit: Determined means both settled or established, and firm of purpose.

blocks.note: an outer cover, as on a book or a boiler

annotation.surface: The jacket of a suit.
annotation.walkthrough: Both words look like clothing; the suit is a lawsuit and the jacket is a covering.
annotation.definitionFit: A case is both a lawsuit and a protective outer covering.

entries.clue: Fully loaded vessel finally leaves port (4)

annotation.surface: A fully loaded ship finally sets sail from port.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Finally' seems to describe the ship at last departing; it picks the last letter of 'vessel'. ADEN is a port in Yemen.
annotation.definitionFit: Aden is a major seaport in Yemen.

entries.clue: Make sweet pop — one expects it for gifts (5,5)

blocks.note: to sugar something is to sweeten it

annotation.surface: Sweetening the fizzy drink, and a hint about a generous benefactor.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pop' reads as a fizzy drink to sweeten, but it is dad. The definition is saucy: a sugar daddy lavishes gifts and expects 'it' in return.
annotation.definitionFit: A sugar daddy is an older man who gives presents to a younger partner in return for companionship or sex.

entries.clue: Becoming an oil billionaire almost, in Guinea (7)

indicatorNotes.almost: take GETTY without its last letter

blocks.note: J. Paul Getty, the oil magnate, less his last letter
G is the abbreviation for guinea, an old British coin worth 21 shillings

annotation.surface: Striking it rich in oil in the African country of Guinea.
annotation.walkthrough: Guinea looks like the country; it is the old British coin, abbreviated G. 'Becoming' is the definition, as in getting rich.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the sense of turning into something: getting tired is becoming tired.

entries.clue: Elitist brought back fine art from Japan (6)

indicatorNotes.brought back: SNOB is turned to read backwards

blocks.note: A1 means first-rate, fine, written with the letter I for the 1

annotation.surface: A snob returns from Japan with some fine art.
annotation.walkthrough: A1 is written AI in crosswords, so 'fine' gives two letters. 'Art from Japan' is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Bonsai is the Japanese art of growing miniature trees in pots.

entries.clue: Too big, old and fat, nearly blocking threshold (9)

indicatorNotes.blocking: LAR sits inside VERGE, blocking the way

blocks.note: on the verge of is on the threshold of
LARD less its last letter, placed inside VERGE

annotation.surface: Someone old and fat can barely get through the doorway.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Threshold' suggests a doorway the fat figure blocks; it gives VERGE, the edge of something.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the prefix over- means excessively, so the word says larger than it should be.

indicatorNotes.reported: what is said aloud, not what is written

blocks.note: trunk is the body; an eight is a rowing crew

annotation.surface: Rowers are said to have trim, fit bodies.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Trim' looks like an adjective describing the rowers' bodies; it is the verb meaning cut short. An eight is a racing boat with eight rowers.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the verb: both mean cutting something shorter by lopping off an end.

indicatorNotes.cryptic: FUN written in a puzzling way, so rearranged

annotation.surface: A witty crossword setter lets loose a fun cryptic.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is about a crossword setter publishing a fun cryptic. Each word is jumbled separately, then the two are joined.
annotation.definitionFit: To unfetter is to free from chains, to release.

indicatorNotes.dressed: IN SILK is dressed, arranged, into a new order

annotation.surface: A city gent wearing silk.
annotation.walkthrough: 'City man dressed in silk' reads as a banker in fine clothes; 'dressed' means arranged, as a shop window is dressed.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the Finnish capital is one instance of a city.

entries.clue: Short rugby player in an exacting role? (7)

blocks.note: a lock is a forward in the second row of a rugby scrum

annotation.surface: A short rugby player asked to take on a demanding position.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Role' seems to be a position on the pitch; it is a stage part. Shylock, in The Merchant of Venice, exacts his pound of flesh.
annotation.definitionFit: Shylock is the moneylender in Shakespeare's Merchant of Venice who insists on exacting his bond.

indicatorNotes.eating: the insect swallows the wood, holding it inside

blocks.note: ash is a wood, placed inside FLY

annotation.surface: A noisy woodworm-like insect munching timber.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Loud' looks like the insect's noise; it describes garish clothes.
annotation.definitionFit: Loud clothes are flashy: showy and garish.

entries.clue: Trouble recalling a name is worrying (7)

indicatorNotes.worrying: the letters are worried, shaken about

annotation.surface: Being unable to remember someone's name is a worry.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole surface describes forgetting a name, which is a small dose of the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Amnesia is loss of memory, trouble recalling things.

entries.clue: Author wary about getting into difficulty (10)

indicatorNotes.getting into: the rearranged letters go inside PLIGHT

blocks.note: a plight is a difficulty, split around the rest

annotation.surface: A writer cautious about getting into trouble.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a nervous author; 'about' is not 'concerning' but a sign to rearrange WARY.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a dramatist is one kind of author, the kind who writes for the stage.

indicatorNotes.not primarily: drop the first letter of TRIP

blocks.note: TRIP, a fall, without its first letter
printers call an en space a nut

annotation.surface: Autumn, which is not mainly the season for nuts.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fall' and 'season' look like autumn; season is the verb meaning mature, as timber is seasoned. A nut is printers' slang for an en.
annotation.definitionFit: To season wood or cheese is to let it mature, to ripen.

entries.clue: US poet’s grit when speaking out (4)

indicatorNotes.when speaking out: the word is said aloud, not written

blocks.note: to grit your teeth is to gnash them; the G is silent

annotation.surface: An American poet showing determination when he makes a speech.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Grit' looks like the noun, courage; it is the verb, as in grit your teeth. Ogden Nash was an American writer of comic verse.
annotation.definitionFit: Ogden Nash was a US poet known for his light verse.

indicatorNotes.about: 'about' means around, so the shortened criticism is placed around the nothing

blocks.note: stick is criticism, as in taking stick; last letter dropped

annotation.surface: Dispassionate criticism that mostly amounts to nothing.
annotation.walkthrough: Stick is British slang for criticism, as in 'giving someone stick'.
annotation.definitionFit: A stoic person bears hardship without showing emotion.

entries.clue: Cruel being rejected for this reason (4)

blocks.note: an ogre is a cruel creature

annotation.surface: Someone is turned away for being cruel.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cruel being rejected' reads as a cruel person getting the brush-off; 'being' is a noun, a creature.
annotation.definitionFit: A Latin loanword meaning therefore, so it marks a conclusion drawn for the reason just given.

blocks.note: a declaration, as of faith or innocence
a line of work, a trade or calling

annotation.surface: An insurance claim line to phone.
annotation.walkthrough: Two unrelated senses: to profess is to claim, and one's line is one's trade.
annotation.definitionFit: A profession is both a declaration or claim and an occupation.

indicatorNotes.leader has departed: the first letter of BOLD goes

blocks.note: bold means brave; its first letter is dropped

annotation.surface: A heroic former chief has died.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Brave leader' reads as a warrior chief; brave is an adjective and 'leader' is its first letter.
annotation.definitionFit: In the sense of one-time rather than aged, as with an old flame or an old boss.

indicatorNotes.off: the letters have gone off, gone wrong

annotation.surface: Finishing a week's holiday worn out.
annotation.walkthrough: 'A week off' looks like a holiday; 'off' tells you to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: A near synonym in the tired sense: drained of strength, as after a long illness.

entries.clue: Small screw regularly holds leather in position (6)

indicatorNotes.regularly: take every other letter of 'screw': C and E
indicatorNotes.holds: S and CE hold the leather between them

blocks.note: to tan hide is to make leather

annotation.surface: A little screw keeps a piece of leather in place.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In position' looks like the end of the screw's job; 'in' is a link and 'position' is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym covering both the way you stand and the view you take on an issue.
